title: Weight preservation for Fibonacci recurrences
statement:
Let $F_m$ be the set of periodic sequences from the Fibonacci recurrence or its parity transform with initial condition $(a_0,a_1)\in(\mathbb Z/m\mathbb Z)^2$, taken modulo $m$. For a divisor $d$ of a composite modulus $m$, define the weight of a period $q$ of length $\ell_q$ in $F_d$ by

$$
w_d(q)=\frac{\ell_q}{d^2}.
$$

If $q_d\in F_d$ extends to periods $q_m^{(1)},\ldots,q_m^{(k)}\in F_m$ reducing to $q_d$ modulo $d$, **Weight Preservation of Fibonacci Recurrences.**

$$
w_d(q_d)=\sum_{i=1}^k w_m(q_m^{(i)}).
$$

Thus the total weight of every period is conjectured to be conserved under extension from $d$ to $m$; the supplied text gives examples but no resolution status.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.24882

Status: **open** according to the source (as of October 2025).
source_name: Marc T. Pudelko, “Modular Periodicity of Random Initialized Recurrences”, arXiv:2510.24882 (2026).
